citation: Hitchcock, J., Dimino, J., Kurki, A., Wilkins, C., & Gersten, R. (2011). The Impact of Collaborative Strategic Reading on the Reading Comprehension of Grade 5 Students in Linguistically Diverse Schools. Final Report (NCEE 2011-4001). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education.
design: Cluster RCT, assignment = classroom/teacher within school (Teacher/Class). Within each linguistically diverse grade-5 school, social-studies classrooms were randomly assigned to CSR (teachers trained in Collaborative Strategic Reading via a 2-day initial training + 4 follow-up coaching sessions, then delivering CSR in their classes) vs business-as-usual control. One school-year implementation. Subject = reading comprehension; grade 5 (registry band 3-6). Final analytic sample: 26 schools, 74 classrooms/teachers (37 CSR, 37 control), 5 districts in Oklahoma & Texas, 1,355 students (681 CSR, 674 control). Low-SES (FRPL ~72%), high ELL. Impacts estimated via 3-level HLM (students in classrooms in schools), pretest-/covariate-adjusted, with multiple imputation (10 datasets) for missing data; report uses Hedges' g as the standardized effect size.
problems: The report directly reports Hedges' g for each contrast, so g values are taken verbatim (g=0.05 primary). The single confirmatory/primary student-achievement outcome is the GRADE composite reading comprehension score (Table 4-1, p.44); its three subscales (vocabulary, sentence comprehension, passage comprehension) feed the composite but are NOT reported as separate impact estimates, so no subscale effect sizes exist to extract. The two FC-ELL / non-ELL contrasts (Table 4-4, p.46) are EXPLORATORY non-randomized subgroups (estimated only on the subset of schools where both groups were present in treatment & control), so outcome_role=subgroup and is_full_sample=false; they are included for completeness but the meta-analysis contrast is the full-sample g=0.05. The text on p.43 says 'two-level HLM' for the confirmatory model while the exec summary (p.3) and Appendix P note say 'three-level HLM (students in classrooms in schools)'; the Q-1 output and design clearly use a 3-level structure, so cluster_adjusted=true regardless. No single design-effect ICC is reported (multilevel model used instead, with per-school CSR slopes pooled), so icc left null per spec (never guess). All impacts pretest-adjusted (pretest GRADE score + language status + teacher Spanish fluency covariates). g_se/g_var derived by scaling the report's raw-metric impact SE by g/impact (i.e. dividing the SE by the same standardizing SD the authors used); these SEs come from the cluster-adjusted HLM so they already account for clustering. Teacher/classroom fidelity and instruction-practice outcomes are not student achievement and were skipped.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CSR (teachers trained in Collaborative Strategic Reading: 2-day initial training + 4 coaching sessions) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: GRADE (Group Reading Assessment and Diagnostic Evaluation) composite reading comprehension score (vocabulary + sentence comprehension + passage comprehension subscales)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring, end of one school-year implementation)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's directly-stated Hedges' g = 0.05 taken verbatim (Table 4-1). It is the model-based HLM impact (0.66 GRADE points, SE 0.40) standardized by the pooled GRADE SD (implied standardizing SD ~13.2). Hedges J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1353 gives J = 0.99945 (~1), so the reported g already reflects the small-sample correction. g_se = impact_se * (g/impact) = 0.40 * (0.05/0.66) = 0.0303; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.000918. SE is from the 3-level cluster-adjusted HLM, so it accounts for clustering.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.44, Table 4-1 (Estimated impact of CSR intervention on reading comprehension); also Exec Summary p.3 and Chapter 5 Summary p.46
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY confirmatory contrast and the one used for the meta-analysis. Mean estimated impact 0.66 GRADE points (SE 0.40), p = 0.11, 95% CI (-0.15, 1.44); not statistically significant. Means are regression-adjusted for pretest GRADE, language status, and teacher Spanish fluency, from 10 multiply-imputed datasets. n_clusters = 74 classrooms/teachers (37 CSR + 37 control) across 26 schools. Treatment effect was not uniform across schools (F = 1.68, p = 0.02, Table Q-2). Nine sensitivity analyses (Tables 4-2/4-3) gave g = 0.01-0.07, all non-significant, robust to the confirmatory result. No follow-up wave beyond the one-year posttest.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CSR vs control - EXPLORATORY subgroup: former & current English language learner (FC-ELL) students
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring, end of one school-year implementation)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's directly-stated Hedges' g = 0.08 taken verbatim (Table 4-4). Impact 0.94 GRADE points (SE 1.30) standardized by the pooled GRADE SD (implied ~11.75). g_se = impact_se * (g/impact) = 1.30 * (0.08/0.94) = 0.1106; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.012242.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.46, Table 4-4 (Effect of CSR on GRADE composite scores, FC-ELL row); p.45 text
effect_sizes.notes: EXPLORATORY, non-randomized subgroup (FC-ELL students only), estimated on the subset of 23 schools / 66 teachers / 1,199 students where both FC-ELL and non-ELL students were present in treatment and control classrooms, with equal weighting. p = 0.47, 95% CI (-1.62, 3.51); not significant. Not the full-sample contrast - included only for completeness.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CSR vs control - EXPLORATORY subgroup: non-ELL students
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring, end of one school-year implementation)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's directly-stated Hedges' g = 0.06 taken verbatim (Table 4-4). Impact 0.69 GRADE points (SE 0.57) standardized by the pooled GRADE SD (implied ~11.5). g_se = impact_se * (g/impact) = 0.57 * (0.06/0.69) = 0.0496; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.002462.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.46, Table 4-4 (Effect of CSR on GRADE composite scores, Non-ELL row); p.45-46 text
effect_sizes.notes: EXPLORATORY, non-randomized subgroup (non-ELL students only), same 23-school subset as the FC-ELL row, equal weighting. p = 0.22, 95% CI (-0.42, 1.81); not significant. The differential (interaction) effect between FC-ELL and non-ELL was 0.25 (SE 1.13, p = 0.82) - no differential impact. Not the full-sample contrast - included only for completeness.
